title: Apply declared artifact verdicts to foreground observations without an Engram trace
outcome: A matched declared foreground command is judged from its original declared artifact even when its project has no Engram observation trace, preserving the artifact-owned verdict contract and honest missing-binding reasons.
acceptance: The cause is recorded from code: the call path by which a matched declared foreground command, in a project without an Engram observation trace, settles its run row without consulting its declared artifact (plain END). Claude review result 364c264d is cited.

For a matched declared command with no trace, the ordinary row is judged by the EXISTING legacy observed-check rules in docs/features/declared-test-commands.md, applied to the originally matched declared artifact and the observed exit through the existing judge. PASS requires exit 0 and a valid PASS artifact. A non-zero exit is FAIL. With exit 0, a FAIL artifact is FAIL, and a missing, invalid or incomplete artifact is UNKNOWN with the named reason. A missing or unknown exit is never PASS. When no original artifact binding exists, the row ends UNKNOWN with a named missing-binding reason, and nothing is reconstructed from current files. No new exit or credit condition, and no change to the native-verification route. Commands that are not declared, and projects that do have a trace, behave as before.

Deterministic tests cover a no-trace project with a declared foreground command: PASS artifact with exit 0, PASS artifact with a non-zero exit, FAIL artifact, a missing or invalid artifact, a missing exit, and the no-binding case. They also show that termal_resume_after_test_runs delivers the same verdict. The independent review pair has no outstanding Medium-or-higher finding, and the full gate passes on the exact committed input.

completion.summary: No-trace declared foreground observations judge the original artifact with the existing exit-aware rules and matching wait verdict; landed d3499b97 with final review and both exact-tree FULLs passed.
